blocks.x: Clienteling copilot for flagship associates — client-facing selling time up 31% and repeat-purchase rate up 13%
a luxury group whose associates carried client knowledge in leather notebooks and whose flagship traffic had outgrown any notebook. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter measured the craft: top associates maintaining 200+ client relationships from memory, 44% repeat-purchase rate among clienteled customers, and new associates needing two years to build what memory couldn't transfer.
Purchase history, preferences and fit lived in systems the associates never saw during a client conversation. Preparation happened after hours or not at all.

We built the clienteling copilot around taste and discretion: unified client profiles spanning purchases, alterations and stated preferences, pre-visit briefs assembled with next-best-suggestions grounded in actual inventory, associate notes captured in-conversation by voice and structured for the next visit, and privacy gates making every data use explicit and auditable. The notebook became a system; the relationship stayed human.
